name: Metaconceptual Art Knowledge Graph
description: Canonical, machine-readable knowledge graph for Metaconceptual Art. Each node carries a stable site ID and, where it corresponds to a real concept, person, or movement, a Wikidata QID plus the art-domain authority IDs (Getty ULAN for people, Getty AAT for concepts, Grove Art Online) so the museum connects outward to both the general and the art-specific linked-data graph. The works are also published as a set of CIDOC-CRM-correct Linked Art (API 1.0) records — digital objects, a textual work, a group, a concept, a collection set, and a provenance activity — each with a HAL _links block and served as application/ld+json. The dataset distinguishes origin from publication: Sun & Rain Works was established in 2005, Metaconceptual Art was created as a movement in 2007, 2009 receipts and metadata are treated as early-work evidence, and 2026 is the public linked-data publication layer.

nodes.label: The Website Itself
nodes.description: The public page treated as the artwork: a surface where language, navigation, metadata, revision, and viewing conditions become material.

nodes.label: Eight Sentences On Metaconceptual Art
nodes.description: A sentence sequence after Sol LeWitt framing Metaconceptual Art as a field of form, institution, market, history, medium, access, and life.

nodes.label: www.wtfisart.com
nodes.description: A born-digital Metaconceptual Art work: a website built and owned by Sun & Rain Works around 2009, named by this collection's origin claim as the work of the 2009 engagement, and realising the studio's concept of the auction as artwork.

nodes.label: Construction of the Museum as Concept
nodes.description: The museum appears inside the artwork as something still being built: institutional authority shown as architecture, ornament, labor, and frame.

nodes.label: Art Market Reform
nodes.description: An image study that treats art, price, reform, and institutional display as one unstable field.

nodes.label: Art Tax
nodes.description: A titled work naming a proposal that art sales be taxed, to press for accountability, transparency and regulation in the art market. Named with Art Market Reform in the studio's 2013 letter to a university museum, which is the only source for it held here; no image or text of the work is held.

nodes.label: Art is Capital
nodes.description: A painting lettered 'Art is Capital', known from one photograph the studio published on its own website, captured by the Internet Archive on 2014-12-18 and again on 2016-01-11. No image is published here and no medium, measurement or date of making is recorded.

nodes.label: What Hedge Funds ?!
nodes.description: A painting lettered 'what hedge funds ?', known from one photograph on the studio's own website, captured by the Internet Archive on 2014-12-18 and again on 2016-01-11. The capture dates the photograph, not the making.

nodes.label: Eightfold Sprocket
nodes.description: A diagrammatic emblem for the eight-sentence proposition set: repetition, rotation, and system held in a compact visual sign.

nodes.label: Movement Graph
nodes.description: The knowledge graph treated as an artwork: relations, authorities, claims, and viewers arranged as a walkable system.

nodes.label: Proof of Movement: Metaconceptual Art
nodes.description: A citable linked-open-data record defining the evidence standard for Metaconceptual Art as a natural, credible, and valid movement.

nodes.label: The auction as artwork (concept)
nodes.description: A Metaconceptual Art work that Sun & Rain Works designates in connection with its 2009 Sotheby's Photographs auction engagement (sale N08533), where it consigned an Ansel Adams photograph (lot 16). A readymade-logic designation asserted by the artist, not a witnessed live-creation event; the catalogue does not name Sun & Rain Works. Two associated works: www.wtfisart.com and WTF is Ansel Adams.

nodes.label: WTF is Ansel Adams
nodes.description: A Metaconceptual Art work Sun & Rain Works designates around its consignment of the Ansel Adams photograph (lot 16) to Sotheby's Photographs, 2009 — a conceptual designation asserted by the artist, not a witnessed performance. Companion to www.wtfisart.com.

nodes.label: www.wtfisart.com — Reconstruction
nodes.description: A nine-page website built in 2026 that reconstructs the 2009 site www.wtfisart.com from the WTFIA source documents and from the surviving HTML, stylesheet and Dreamweaver template of Growing Aloha, an unrelated 2009 site by the same hands. The text is transcribed from the 2009 documents; the page structure, titles and front-page wording are the reconstruction's own. No HTML from the original site survives, and this is not evidence that the site was ever live.

nodes.label: Art Notes
nodes.description: A framed studio notice board carrying handwritten notes, the first of which reads 'WTF is Art ?!', alongside the name 'Sun and Rain Works' and pinned art-market press cuttings. Evidenced by one studio-held photograph whose camera-written Exif gives 2012-11-30; its content places it no earlier than 20 May 2010 and its camera model no earlier than 2011. A self-reported date on a studio file, not independently notarized, and no evidence of the asserted 2007 origin.

nodes.label: Evidence archive: auction engagement (2009)
nodes.description: A record describing the private archive Sun & Rain Works holds for its 2009 Sotheby's engagement — 2008 correspondence, the consignment of an Ansel Adams photograph (lot 16), domain/hosting receipts for www.wtfisart.com, photographs, and metadata. These evidence the artist identity, the engagement, and the website's date; they do not record a witnessed live-creation event. Independently verifiable: the public catalogue lot (N08533).

nodes.label: Conceptual claim to art at auction (2009)
nodes.description: The artist's asserted conceptual designation: that Sun & Rain Works framed its 2009 Sotheby's auction engagement as art. Presented as the artist's position, not an adjudicated historical fact; makes no 'first in history' claim and disputes no later artist or event.

nodes.label: Evidence archive: the WTFIA source folder for www.wtfisart.com (2008-2009)
nodes.description: A record describing the WTFIA folder: the source material Sun & Rain Works assembled for www.wtfisart.com — four Word documents dated January to March 2009 (an art-market press compilation, a photographer note, and the two dealer-network directories built as the site's link content) with sets of art-market, art-historical, and photographic reference images dated 2008-2009. These evidence what was made for the site and the source context for the Art Market Reform image study. The folder holds no HTML, so it does not record what the site published or when it went live. Dates are self-reported by file and document metadata, not independently notarized.

nodes.label: Sun and Rain Works in a market's membership records (2005, 2006, 2008)
nodes.description: The Eugene Saturday Market, running weekly since 1970 and the oldest continuously operating open-air crafts market in the United States, states from its own membership records that Sun and Rain Works was a member in 2005, 2006 and 2008. Its rule is that goods are made and sold by their maker, so this attests a working art business selling at its stalls. The earliest attestation of the studio name in this collection and the only one made by a third party about a date before 2011. It says nothing about Metaconceptual Art. Held as a screenshot of the market's 2024 reply, so reported rather than verified, but re-checkable with the market.

nodes.label: The executed Sotheby's consignment agreement (March 2009)
nodes.description: The instrument of consignment itself. Sotheby's sent a scanned agreement on 2009-03-18 saying a signed copy was required before the photograph could be sold; the studio returned a signed PDF the next day. Six pages on Sotheby's letterhead dated 18-Mar-2009, naming the studio principal as consignor and signed by him and countersigned for Sotheby's, plus one page of identity verification. Held, checksummed, and deliberately unpublished: the agreement binds the consignor not to disclose its terms without Sotheby's written consent, and one page is a government identity document. This closes the consignor-of-record question that the catalogue, which names no consignor, leaves open. The agreement is in the studio principal's own name, which is how a sole proprietorship contracts; the opening approach of August 2008 disclosed Sun and Rain Works to Sotheby's as exactly that.

nodes.label: Approach to the Ansel Adams organisation (8-9 August 2008)
nodes.description: Two emails about twenty minutes apart on the evening of 2008-08-08, to a named representative at the Ansel Adams organisation, two days before the approach to a museum and five before Sotheby's. One carries eight loose frames; the other carries San Francisco.zip itself, byte-identical to the archive sent to the auction house six days later. Both presuppose earlier telephone contact, and the body they identify is the one the museum letter miscalls the Ansel Adams Museum in San Francisco. The archive message retains original Hotmail headers and is the better-evidenced of the two; the other was rewritten by a later platform, and their relative order is not settled. The earliest documents held in this collection. Signed For the Love of Art. Name neither Sun and Rain Works nor Metaconceptual Art.

nodes.label: Approach to a museum photography department (11 August 2008)
nodes.description: An email of 2008-08-11 to the photography department of the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, three days before the approach to Sotheby's and under the same subject line. Introduces the writer as an artist and sole proprietor of Sun and Rain Works, describes a previously unknown Ansel Adams photograph then believed to date from 1946, and says he thought this happening might be of some interest to the museum. No longer the earliest dated document in this collection - two messages of 2008-08-08 to the Ansel Adams organisation precede it by two days - but still the earliest dated use of the studio name, which neither earlier message carries. It reports contact with a named person at what it calls the Ansel Adams Museum in San Francisco, an institution that did not exist; the earlier message identifies the body actually approached. No reply is held and no museum response is evidenced. The word happening carries a conceptual reading and an ordinary one, and this collection chooses neither.

nodes.label: The Sotheby's consignment correspondence (2008-2009)
nodes.description: An outbound email of 2008-08-14 to a specialist in Sotheby's Photographs department, with a 3 MB zip of the eleven documentation frames of 2008-08-08. Names Sun and Rain Works as an art business and its principal as an artist in Eugene, Oregon, and describes the print as owned and being researched. An earlier version of this entry called this the earliest dated use of the studio name in this collection; that was wrong on its own terms, since the museum letter of 2008-08-11 carries the same name three days sooner. Two further messages of March 2009 carry the consignment agreement: the department writes about 'your photograph' and chases the signed agreement posted in February, and the studio replies that it holds the sheet and will fax it back. The attachment is held and is byte-identical to the studio's copies; the messages are held as screenshots and are reported, not verified. The frame composing the print with Warhol's philosophy was among those transmitted.

nodes.label: The staged photographs of the print (autumn 2008)
nodes.description: Seventeen studio-held photographs that stage the retrieval of the Adams print from a storage unit, present it to the camera, record its verso, and show it taken out of its frame at a framer's workshop. The camera wrote no date; the files were processed on a Mac on 2008-11-25 by its clock, and no earlier than 2008-09-15 by the software versions they record, which dates them before the sale. Sun and Rain Works states they were made by its art assistants as documentation of WTF is Ansel Adams. They were not sent to the museum or the auction house, the images are not published, and checksums only are given.

nodes.label: The studio's websites as captured by the Internet Archive (2013-2016)
nodes.description: Third-party captures of two domains the studio ran. wtfisart.com on 2013-07-20 shows only 'Under Construction'; on 2014-12-18 and 2016-01-11 it shows a Drupal install whose menu reads 'Art Market Reform is a happening' and whose text carries the line handwritten on the Art Notes board, while stating 'No front page content has been created yet'. sunandrainworks.com on 2016-01-26 and 2016-03-27 carries the eight defining characteristics in full, in the same wording as the 2012 posting. The capture dates are the Archive's and are the evidence; the pages' own CMS stamps are not. No capture mentions the 2009 auction, and the domain passed to another owner from 2016. The record also covers the studio's Flickr account, where nine photographs bear on this collection: the Art Notes board and a painting titled What Hedge Funds, both publicly posted 2013-06-02, three months before the museum letter; and six works posted 2014-05-18, among them the Art Market Reform and Art Tax paintings the letter names, three of which carry the public tag 'Metaconceptual'. The 2014 group postdates the letter and is consistent with it rather than evidence for it. None of the files carries Exif, so the upload stamp is the only date each has. The profile biography states the lot 16 designation but carries no date.

nodes.label: The registrar's receipts for the studio's domains (2009-2016)
nodes.description: A domain registrar's billing record for the studio's account, held as the registrar's export and forty-two PDF invoices and published here as checksums only. It registers WTFISART.COM on 2009-03-16 at 00:45:06 UTC, buys hosting for it at 01:07:15 the same night, and pays that hosting monthly to 2009-12-15 - fourteen days before the Sotheby's sale of 30 March 2009 and the nine months after it. A blogging product bought in the same transaction was refunded thirty-five minutes later, which accounts for the studio's memory of an early blog. GROWINGALOHA.COM was registered 2009-01-04 and renewed 2010-01-05. The invoices run on to 2016-01-05: WTFISART.COM was re-registered 2011-10-16, in the same bulk order as METACONCEPTUALART.COM, and renewed through to 2016. The record says nothing about what was served at the domain. Every invoice names Sun and Rain Works in its Bill To block; an earlier version of this summary said the opposite, and that statement is withdrawn.

nodes.label: Documentation photographs of the Ansel Adams print (August 2008)
nodes.description: Eleven photographs exposed in one session on 2008-08-08, carrying camera-written Exif, documenting a matted Ansel Adams print in the studio's possession - recto, mount, verso, and a close-up of the verso credit block. The verso markings agree in four particulars with the public Sotheby's catalogue entry for sale N08533, lot 16: the American Trust Company credit stamp, the 1-SF- negative-number series, the inked 'Wells Fargo Bank' annotation over the struck-through article, and the handwritten title. One frame composes the print with a volume of Warhol's philosophy. Independently checkable against the public catalogue; the consignor of record is evidenced separately, by the 2009 consignment correspondence.

nodes.label: Correspondence declaring Metaconceptual Art to a museum (2013)
nodes.description: An email thread of 2013-09-12 in which the studio principal set out Metaconceptual Art in writing to the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art: the field, its eight defining characteristics, 'Art Market Reform' and 'Art Tax' as works, Sun & Rain Works as the business, and the May 2009 Sotheby's lot 16 consignment as a performance act. The museum acknowledged receipt. Four independent header timestamps, two written by Yahoo's servers and copied into the university's Exchange headers, corroborate the date, and in July 2026 the museum retrieved the message from its own archive and supplied it on request, so the record is institutionally retained rather than studio-held. Asked at the same time, the museum found no email from the studio dated 2009. The earliest written declaration of the field the studio has produced - a declaration, not an independent finding, and no evidence of the asserted 2007 origin.

nodes.label: Public postings of Metaconceptual Art (2011-2012)
nodes.description: Two public postings under the account LIVINGART8, still readable and set never to expire. 'The Art World is Flat', 2011-11-28, introduces its poem as a metaconceptual Art poem, treating the term as already settled. 'MetaConceptual Art', 2012-11-22, sets out the eight defining characteristics, which agree word for word with the Eight Sentences published here fourteen years later. Dates are assigned by the platform and the paste bodies are fixed once posted, so this is the earliest evidence in the collection that needs no access to the private archive. Both link to a Sun & Rain Works page on Facebook.

nodes.label: A photograph of two studio works inscribed 'W.T.F. is Art ?' (8 November 2011)
nodes.description: A camera-phone original, Exif intact, recording its capture as 2011-11-08 12:18:15, with the phone's own file name giving the same minute. It shows a board inscribed 'Helping the Art Historians of the future to keep their Employment (Here and Now)' lying on a large handwritten sheet whose right-hand edge reads 'W.T.F. is Art ?', punctuated as a question. Neither physical work survives, by the studio's account. The board was the foundation of the digital work ArtHistoriansOTheFuture, posted publicly to the studio's Flickr account on 2013-06-02 and byte-identical to the studio's held copy; its words recur in the studio's letter of 2013-09-12 to a university art museum, and the photograph falls twenty-three days after WTFISART.COM was re-registered. The titles, Helping the Art Historians of the future and Dancing with Mummies, and the latter's reference to Thomas Hoving, are the studio's account. The date is the file's own and not notarized; the record does not date either work's making, shows nothing public, and says nothing about 2009. The image is held and published as a checksum only.

nodes.label: A painted postcard inscribed 'For the Love of Art' and signed 2008 (photographed 2011)
nodes.description: A small work made on a museum postcard: the picture side painted over in acrylic and ink and signed 'Joe Chirum 08', the address side inscribed 'For the Love of Art, these tulips are beautiful! Almost as good as in real life', with 'J.M.C. 08' and the postscript 'Double the Fun'. It is known from one photograph, taken on 2011-11-16 by the same camera phone as the 'W.T.F. is Art ?' photograph of eight days earlier. That file is a cropped and renamed derivative rather than the camera's original, so its date is the file's account at one remove; the 2008 date is written on the work by its maker. The record fixes only that the work existed, framed, by November 2011.

nodes.label: A photograph of a shop sign reading META, Italy (27 February 2012)
nodes.description: A camera original with Exif intact, a night photograph of an illuminated Italian shop sign reading META SUPERNEGOZI, captured 2012-02-27 21:41:53 with no GPS; the held file's name says March 2012, which is when it was filed rather than taken. The sign is an Italian retail chain's, meta with a grave accent being Italian for half, and the record asserts no connection between that business and the studio, nor any relation to any later corporation of the name. The studio states it photographed the sign because the word answered to Metaconceptual Art; that is its account, given in 2026, and the photograph does not evidence the asserted 2007 naming.

nodes.label: Metaconceptual Art
nodes.description: A self-defined movement concept created by Sun & Rain Works in 2007: art that treats art, its institutions, markets, archives, viewers, metadata, and provenance as the material of the work.

nodes.label: Conceptual art
nodes.description: Contemporary art movement that shifts attention from the handmade object to the idea.

nodes.label: Institutional critique
nodes.description: Artistic practice that treats the museum, market, gallery, and frame as the material of the work.

nodes.label: Systems art
nodes.description: Art influenced by cybernetics and systems theory, foregrounding relation, process, and feedback over the discrete object.

nodes.label: Internet art
nodes.description: Art that uses the website, protocol, page, and browser as its artistic site.

nodes.label: Found object / readymade
nodes.description: Art created from undisguised, often modified, objects designated as art by context rather than craft.

nodes.label: Provenance
nodes.description: The traceable chronology of ownership, custody, and lineage of an object, idea, or claim.

nodes.label: Knowledge graph
nodes.description: An information repository structured as a graph of entities and relationships, the form the meta-museum takes.

nodes.label: Semantic Web
nodes.description: Extension of the Web that enables data exchange through shared identifiers, vocabularies, and machine-readable relations.

nodes.label: Linked open data
nodes.description: Linked data available under an open license, used here as the public evidence medium for the movement's claims.

nodes.label: Sol LeWitt
nodes.description: American artist (1928-2007); his Sentences on Conceptual Art establish the sentence as a conceptual, rule-based unit.

nodes.label: Joseph Kosuth
nodes.description: American conceptual artist (born 1945); art as inquiry into the conditions of art.

nodes.label: Marcel Duchamp
nodes.description: French artist (1887-1968); designation, context, and the readymade.

nodes.label: Sotheby's Photographs auction (sale N08533, 2009)
nodes.description: The public auction (sale N08533), carried out by Sotheby's, at which Sun & Rain Works consigned an Ansel Adams photograph (lot 16) and which it treats as the material of the concept of the auction as artwork, realised in the works www.wtfisart.com and WTF is Ansel Adams. The outcome of lot 16 is not established: the public catalogue places the result behind an account login, and no source held here records whether it sold, was bought in, or was withdrawn.

nodes.label: Sotheby's
nodes.description: International auction house (founded 1744) named as the institution that carried out the 2009 Photographs auction (sale N08533). Recorded as context only, with no assertion of authorship, endorsement, or dispute.

nodes.label: Provenance Layer
nodes.description: Tracks authorship, revision, and the lineage of every claim and work.

nodes.label: Viewer
nodes.description: The position that activates meaning by reading, querying, and interpreting the work.

nodes.label: Wikidata Layer
nodes.description: Grounded the semantic layer in Wikidata identifiers and added a live related-concepts query.

nodes.label: Origin Provenance
nodes.description: Machine-readable chronology distinguishing Sun & Rain Works formation in 2005, Metaconceptual Art movement creation in 2007, 2009 early-work evidence, and 2026 linked-data publication.

nodes.label: Recommended Citation
nodes.description: Makes the work formally referenceable.
